s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute pulmonary syndrome in an immunocompromised patient with a history of renal transplant
salient_findings: Bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates on chest radiograph
Bilateral diffuse ground-glass opacities on high-resolution CT of the chest
Positive Pneumocystis jirovecii on Grocott’s methenamine silver stain of BAL fluid
New left upper-zone infiltrates after discontinuation of TMP-SMX
Leukopenia with a total lymphocyte count of 1400/μL and ANC of 1050/μL
key_facts: 36-year-old man with end-stage renal disease secondary to IgA nephropathy
Underwent live-related renal transplant 6 months ago
Maintained on tacrolimus 3.5 mg daily, mycophenolate sodium 720 mg daily, and prednisolone 7.5 mg daily
Presented with a 14-day history of low-grade fever, dry cough, and anorexia
Afebrile on admission with heart rate 88 beats/min, blood pressure 122/76 mm Hg, respiratory rate 28 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air
Bilateral inspiratory crackles on examination
Hemoglobin 14.6 g/dL, total lymphocyte count 9900/μL, absolute neutrophil count 7720/μL, platelets 285 000/μL, serum creatinine 1.05 mg/dL
Arterial blood gas analysis demonstrated PaO₂ 68 mm Hg and an A–a gradient of 22 mm Hg
HIV ELISA was negative
Sputum induction was non-diagnostic
BAL fluid was positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii on Grocott’s methenamine silver stain
Treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and a prednisone taper with clinical and radiographic resolution of infiltrates after 2 weeks
Developed leukopenia after discontinuation of TMP-SMX
Transbronchial lung biopsy showed alveoli filled with inflammatory debris consisting of granulation tissue, interstitial inflammation, and areas of intra-alveolar fibrin deposition
